title: A look inside Latin America’s aura battles
description:
Aura farming has left your phone screen and landed in public squares all over Latin America. Hundreds of people are attending ‘aura battles’ - high-energy public competitions where the only way to win is show just how much raw charisma you have. Laura Garcia from BBC Mundo tells us exactly what it takes to prove your aura. Dani San, who’s been organising aura battles in Chile, tells us what it’s like to watch one unfold.

Plus Mollie Perella from the What in the World team gets a lesson in ‘aura farming’ from Ava Arabian, a content creator from New York.

Email: whatintheworld@bbc.co.uk WhatsApp: +44 330 12 33 22 6 Presenter: Hannah Gelbart Producers: Emily Horler, Benita Barden and Mollie Perella Editor: Verity Wilde
summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討源自網路與電玩文化的「氣場對決」 aura battles 現象。這類活動風靡拉丁美洲並擴散至全球，參加者聚集於公共廣場，透過展示獨特魅力、模仿網路迷因與遊戲動作進行趣味比拚。 BBC 記者 Laura Garcia 與智利活動籌辦者 Dani San 分享了現場盛況，指出活動能讓大眾遠離螢幕、重返公共空間交流。儘管部分網路言論批評其荒謬，且某些地方政府因不了解而實施禁令，但對參與者而言，這是展現自我與凝聚社群的現代舞鬥。節目亦邀請創作者 Ava Arabian 解析「氣場耕耘」 aura farming 與過度裝模作樣 larping 的文化意涵。
summaryEn: This episode explores the phenomenon of 'aura battles'—high-energy public competitions sweeping Latin America and spreading globally. Rooted in internet, gaming, and TikTok culture, these events feature participants facing off in public squares to showcase raw charisma, quirky poses, video game references, and meme-inspired moves rather than conventional dance technique. Host Hannah Gelbart talks with content creator Ava Arabian about 'aura farming' and 'larping,' BBC journalist Laura Garcia about the origin, public reactions, and official pushback surrounding these gatherings, and organizer Dani San about the inclusive, family-friendly atmosphere in Chile designed to bring people together offline.
